dates.altered: Lean-to added in the 18th century (HABS data form; the node's exemplar says c. 1764); major restoration by the Quincy Historical Society in 1897; most windows are replacements with a Federal muntin profile (HABS).
dates.note: The node's exemplar says 1717 and warns that the house is 'often mis-dated to 1663 in popular sources'; the Wikipedia infobox says 1716; the HABS data form of 1979-83 itself prints 'Ca. 1663, with 18th.century lean-to'. Recorded as the register and the node have it, with the survey's own date left standing beside them.

quotes.text: ADAMS, JOHN QUINCY, BIRTHPLACE HABS NO. MA-597 SECONDARY OR COMMON NAMES OF STRUCTURE COMPLETE ADDRESS (DESCRIBE LOCATION FOR RURALSITES) 141 Franklin Street DATE OF CONSTRUCTION (INCLUDESOURCE) ARCHITECT(S) (INCLUDESOURCE) Ca. 1663, with 18th.century lean-to | Samuel Belcher, original owner, was builder
quotes.page: HABS Architectural Data Form, page 1; no page number printed on the form's first sheet

quotes.text: ectangular in shape; measures approx. 36' X 33'
quotes.page: HABS Architectural Data Form, page 1, 'Shape and dimensions of structure'; the leading letter is cut off in the scan

quotes.text: The foundation of granite fieldstone is generally original. The walls of the original house were originally wood stud with brick nngging and rlay mnrtar -infill
quotes.page: HABS Architectural Data Form, page 1, 'Material of construction'

quotes.text: The original house has a purlin system roof, which was raised on its west eleva- tion to accommodate the lean-to. Gable rafters are sawn; lean-to rafters are hand-hewn. Post-and-Beam construction is used. Summer beams on the first floor of the original house run lengthwise, whereas second floor beams run thwartwise. Cornerposts are visible on the inside. Second floor posts are flared.
quotes.page: HABS Architectural Data Form, continuation page; no page marker legible in the extract span

quotes.text: There are two stairways from the first floor to the second. The front stairway, is a winder. The rear stairway is a straight run. A third stairway leads to the gable attic from the second floor- a winder,
quotes.page: HABS Architectural Data Form, page 1, 'Interior features of note'

quotes.text: The main (east) frontispiece is pedimented and pilastered. The west elevation has an early board door with many layers of paint. Most of the windows are replacements having a Federal muntin profile. Roof asphalt covering is over original sheathing, which was laid vertically
quotes.page: HABS Architectural Data Form, page 1, 'Exterior features of note'
